findings.reason: The protected app-local and Accepted native sources implement the standard positional counting formula. For each decimal factor they derive the higher digits, current digit, and lower remainder, add the exact complete-plus-partial-cycle contribution, and advance by one position. The O(log n)-time/O(1)-space code is clear and conventional, so no candidate is justified.

The app-local function and native class method are structurally identical in factor progression, higher/current/lower decomposition, three contribution branches, and total accumulation. Their only difference is the required LeetCode class wrapper.

The legal domain contains at most ten decimal positions, so 1/4/9-digit runtime tiers cannot establish an unbounded scaling verdict. A bounded-domain certificate now proves one constant-work iteration per decimal position, at most ten iterations under n <= 10^9, matching O(log n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

The Approach accurately derives complete cycles and all three partial-cycle cases, explains why summing independent positions neither omits nor duplicates occurrences, and now labels zero and power-of-ten boundaries separately.
